content_of_post_to_comment:
As above. For years, I struggled with lack of self belief, lack of self worth and self love. And still do. At 39.5 I was 3-4 years into my own business, which I never got off the ground as much as others, or as much as I should, because what if I didn't have what it takes? What if I failed.

Still living at home, and hating every second of my life, including certain people around me.

Then my health went pop.

I now spend 3 evenings a week getting my blood cleaned so I won't die. I've had to take medication I would never have willingly taken, accept procedures done to me that I would never have done otherwise, have to answer to people about why I've eaten too much fruit, or some nuts. Have to ask permission if I want an evening off. Can't plan a holiday without arranging dialysis, which means no holidays where I just go get lost. I can't go off grid. I've lost all my freedom.

And before anyone says "oh, a transplant", even that's not freedom, because transplants fail, and I'll have to take medications I would never have willingly taken.

My point is this. After my physical health went, I was kicking myself about not grabbing life by the horns prior to that. I was kicking myself about all the limitations in my head.

I realised I had everything I needed to succeed, to LIVE. Even with family obligations and complications. Even with things I need therapy about. Even with my lack of self belief. All the "in my head" stuff, paled in comparison to losing my physical health.

And it pains me to see people who are healthy, and yet are stuck in their own head, and life is passing them by. Reading motivational book, after motivational book, with nothing changing. Stuck in pain, stuck in harmful patterns, stuck in mediocrity. It pains me to see myself in them, and wishing I could shake them awake. And I don't mean mediocrity as in not being a millionaire. I mean living in the grey. Not adding colour to their lives. Not using the potential they KNOW deep down that they have.

Please don't wait until something happens to you, outside of your control, to shake you awake. Realise that a lot of our suffering is in our mind. Screw whoever put those ideas in your mind that you can't succeed, that you don't have what it takes. You do. Don't wait until you lose the most valuable thing you have, to realise that.
comment: The part about realizing your mental barriers were small compared to losing your health really hit me. It's easy to underestimate the freedom we have when nothing is forcing us to confront our limits. At the same time, I think there's a strange middle ground where fear isn't just an excuse but something people genuinely have to learn to work through. I hope you find ways to reclaim pieces of freedom even within the restrictions you're facing.
